newsitem.title: USA: L.A. power utility sets rate cut for large users.
newsitem.headline: L.A. power utility sets rate cut for large users.

text.p: The Los Angeles Board of Water and Power Commissioners approved on Tuesday a plan to lower electricity rates for large industrial customers served by the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power.

The Board said the rate restructuring will result in lower electricity bills for 70 percent of those customers. Residential customers, along with small and medium business customers, are not affected by the proposal.
Along with the 70 percent of large customers receiving lower rates, about 20 percent of LADWP's business customers will have rate increases of under 5 percent, the board said.

Most of the cutomers receiving increases larger than 5 percent are small usage customers who have not been paying their share of the electric system's cost, according to Carolyn Green, president of the board.
The plan will be sent to the city council and the mayor for final approval.
